name: Crimson Crest
description: Crimson Crest is named for the rust-red mountain chains that dominate its equatorial band, their iron-rich peaks catching the light of a pale amber sun. Vast temperate forests blanket the lowlands between these ranges, their canopies shifting from deep emerald to burnt sienna with the seasons. Rivers of clear water carve through rift valleys so deep that their floors remain in perpetual twilight.

The air carries the scent of mineral-rich soil and the distant calls of winged creatures that roost among the crimson peaks. At dawn, mist rises from the rift valleys in slow, rolling curtains that glow pink in the early light. Evenings bring a stillness broken only by the crystalline resonance of wind passing through exposed cavern mouths in the mountainsides.

Survey teams discovered elaborate ruins carved into the deepest rift valley walls, their geometric patterns unlike any known civilization's architectural language. The ruins are silent, but an intermittent signal pulses from somewhere beneath the largest mountain range, repeating a pattern that defies cryptographic analysis. No one has determined who built here or why they left.

Crimson Crest's breathable atmosphere and rich biosphere make it a prime candidate for colonization, but the xenoarchaeological significance of the ruins has placed it under academic embargo. Competing research institutions vie for exclusive survey rights while independent prospectors eye the planet's substantial iron and biological resource deposits. The signal grows fractionally stronger each year, and some researchers believe it is counting down to something.
